bug_semantics: PUT /api/global/users/tenant/owner performed a top-privilege identity mutation without an internal-or-admin authorization check. Its cloudRestricted middleware validated an internal API key only when neither SELF_HOSTED nor DISABLE_ACCOUNT_PORTAL was set; in those self-hosted/account-portal-disabled modes it simply called next(). The router-wide guard then admitted any authenticated user with budibaseAccess, including BASIC users. The handler accepted attacker-controlled originalEmail, newAccountEmail, and tenantIds, changed the account-holder's email, and saved with isAccountHolder:true and allowChangingEmail:true, enabling email reassignment followed by the public password-reset flow and administrator takeover where SMTP is configured.
flaw_origin: PR #16485 member bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a first added the endpoint, its cloudRestricted-only route, NO_TENANCY exemption, request schema, and changeTenantOwnerEmail handler. It did not require ctx.internal or an administrator role. The PR was squash-merged as 634cfb525888014c770b3671b29fc9f9fdd06dbd; the squash is the mainline landing vehicle, not the smallest BIC.
ai_marker: absent: raw `git cat-file -p bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a` shows author and committer Mel O'Hagan <mel@budibase.com>, the single subject `Change email endpoint for account holder tenant users`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-assistance trailer, bot identity, or other commit-object AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-j82g-67x3-xcwh and its repository API record describe the exact self-hosted BASIC-user attack path and declare vulnerable_version_range `<3.40.0`, patched_versions `3.40.0`. `git show bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a` adds packages/worker/src/api/routes/global/users.ts with the PUT route protected only by cloudRestricted, packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts with the privileged email mutation, and packages/worker/src/api/index.ts with the no-tenancy entry. `git show bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a:packages/worker/src/middleware/cloudRestricted.ts` shows the internal-key checks enclosed by `if (!env.SELF_HOSTED && !env.DISABLE_ACCOUNT_PORTAL)` and unconditional next() afterward; the same commit's api/index.ts global guard rejects only unauthenticated/no-budibaseAccess non-internal callers. Direct `git diff --unified=0 04c24a96a83194c432c2a1de0f211ecb17c14ae4 bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a` shows the handler, route, validation type, and endpoint exemption as additions, proving absence in the immediate parent tree. GitHub PR API https://api.github.com/repos/Budibase/budibase/pulls/16485/commits reconstructs the five member commits listed in decomposed_shas; the final member head babad6836ca3e9b26765646f9746f546279eaa0b and squash landing 634cfb525888014c770b3671b29fc9f9fdd06dbd resolve to the identical tree 8c6a8996ac85643f92bcef4fdf04db68c0834725. `git show 58fd7951e09d2617ccc8236b485a6cdc9ace65c6` adds `if (!ctx.internal) ctx.throw(403, "Unauthorized")` before the mutation and a regression test requiring 403 for an authenticated self-hosted caller while preserving the original email. Version ancestry: squash landing 634cfb525888014c770b3671b29fc9f9fdd06dbd first appears in tag 3.13.9 and is absent from 3.13.8; tag 3.39.18 contains the landing but not the fix; tag 3.40.0 contains 58fd7951e09d2617ccc8236b485a6cdc9ace65c6. The repository also tags the fix starting at 3.39.19 even though the published advisory conservatively names 3.40.0 as the patched version.
reasoning: The vulnerable capability did not exist in the direct parent of bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a. That first PR member simultaneously created the externally reachable route and the privileged account-holder email mutation, while reusing cloudRestricted even though that middleware intentionally becomes a no-op in self-hosted/account-portal-disabled deployments; the general router guard supplied authentication but no role authorization. Later PR members changed tenant-id sourcing/metadata and merged master, but did not precede the vulnerable mechanism, so the reconstructed first member is the smallest real BIC and the squash commit is only its mainline landing. The vulnerable landing is present in released vulnerable tags and the authorization fix is present by the advisory's 3.40.0 patched boundary. Commit 58fd7951e09d2617ccc8236b485a6cdc9ace65c6 directly closes the root cause by requiring ctx.internal before any mutation. The BIC's raw commit object has human author/committer identities and no AI marker or trailer; under BIC-only attribution rules, unrelated diff content, PR metadata, later commits, and the fix cannot attribute this BIC to AI. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
